summary.text: Jesse James is a Republican member of the Wisconsin Senate representing District 23, based in Thorp, elected to the Senate in 2022 after serving in the Assembly from 2018 to 2020.
He chairs the Committee on Mental Health, Substance Abuse Prevention, Children and Families and is vice-chair of the Committee on Judiciary and Public Safety.

paragraphs.text: James was born in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, on April 16, 1972, and is married with four children and two grandchildren.
He graduated from Eau Claire North High School in 1990 and earned an associate degree in police science from Chippewa Valley Technical College in 2001.
The Legislature's page lists him as a small business owner and part-time police officer with the Cadott Police Department, and a state firearms instructor.
It says he served in the U.S. Army Air Defense from 1990 to 1993 and in the U.S. Army Reserves as a medic from 1993 to 1996, and that he is a Persian Gulf War veteran.

He was a National Council of State Legislatures Opioid Fellow in 2022 and is a member of the Child Abuse and Neglect Prevention Board, the Council on Alcohol and Other Drug Abuse, the Council on Military and State Relations and the Human Trafficking Council.
